The Milky Way arches overhead like a river of spilled silver light.
A luminous band of stars pours softly from horizon to horizon.
The great star-river drifts, thick with ancient light and quiet dust.
Aurora folds itself in green and violet across the dreaming sky.
Curtains of green shimmer into violet, breathing slowly overhead.
The aurora drapes the dark in living ribbons of emerald and plum.
A vast full moon hangs impossibly low, heavy and amber-warm.
The moon fills a quarter of the sky, soft as a paper lantern.
Stars streak endlessly downward, silver threads unraveling through the dark.
A hundred falling stars trace slow arcs across the velvet night.
Twin crescent moons float side by side, their horns nearly touching.
Two silver crescents drift apart like parentheses cradling the dark.
A rose-and-teal nebula blooms softly, enormous and slow as breath.
Clouds of rose and teal glow drift like smoke from a gentle fire.
One star burns alone at the zenith, brilliant and perfectly still.
A single star blazes so bright it casts faint shadows below.
Luminous mist drifts in slow veils across the face of the stars.
Pale glowing mist rises and folds, erasing and revealing the sky.
A ring of faintly glowing planets sits low along the horizon's edge.
Seven worlds glow in a soft arc, their colors gentle as sea glass.
The starfield shimmers below as if the ground has become the sky.
Stars reflect in the dark below, the earth dissolved into heaven.
A moon-halo spreads in a pale ring through thin drifting cloud.
Thin cloud softens the moon into a luminous smear of white.
Fireflies rise in slow spirals, vanishing into the waiting stars above.
